CONSENT CALENDAR The recommendations on the following Consent Calendar will be enacted in one motion unless an item is removed from the Calendar. Any member of the public may remove an item by submitting a “PINK” speaker slip to the City Clerk. Each speaker is allowed three (3) minutes to address the City Council. A maximum of two time donations per speaker is allowed (no more than 9 minutes total); the person donating time must be present. Items removed from the Consent Calendar by a Council Member or the public will be considered immediately following the Consent Calendar.

2024-12-11 Item 08D City Council Meeting Schedule 2025
2024-12-11 Item 08D City Council Meeting Schedule 2025-UPDATED
8E.
Professional Consultant Services Agreement between the City of Encinitas and Ascent Environmental, Inc. ("Ascent") to provide a focused amendment to the Resource Management Element of the General Plan pursuant to Senate Bill ("SB") 1425 and Assembly Bill ("AB") 1889. Environmental Considerations: The action before the City Council is not subject to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) pursuant to Section 15060(c)(3) of the CEQA Guidelines since the action is not a "project" pursuant to Section 15378(b)(5). The action involves an organizational or administrative activity of government that will not result in a direct or indirect physical change in the environment. Environmental review would be determined and conducted prior to the adoption of any resulting General Plan amendment. Contact Person: Senior Mobility Planner Jedynak
Authorize the City Manager, in coordination with the City Attorney, to execute a Professional Consultant Services Agreement, in substantial form, for a focused amendment to the Resource Management Element with Ascent, in an amount not-to-exceed $470,687.
2024-12-11 Item 08E Resource Management Contract
8F.
Consideration of a 15-year lease agreement for the use of Encinitas coastal beaches within the California State Lands Commission jurisdiction, in conjunction with the City's Opportunistic Beach Fill Program (OBFP) and Sand Compatibility and Opportunistic Use Program (SCOUP). Environmental Considerations: The recommended action being considered by the City Council is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) because it is not a "project" under Section 15378(b)(5) of the CEQA Guidelines. The action involves an organizational or administrative activity of government that will not result in the direct or indirect physical change in the environment.
The current Mitigated Negative Declaration (MND) prepared and adopted for the OBFP included the Cities of Encinitas, Solana Beach, Coronado, and Imperial Beach in April 2008 (SCH No. 2008021048), and the City adopted a Final Mitigated Negative Declaration to amend the City of Encinitas OBFP in February 2014 (SCH No. 2013111057). There are no changes proposed for the current program at this time, aside from extending the existing permits, including the lease permit through the California State Lands Commission Contact Person: Coastal Zone Program Administrator Mierau
Adopt Resolution No. 2024-128 titled, "A Resolution of the City Council of the City of Encinitas, California, to Authorize the City Manager, or Their Designee, to Execute a 15-Year Lease Agreement with the California State Lands Commission to Allow Continued Sand Nourishment Along the Encinitas Coast, Consistent with the Locations Set Through the Encinitas Opportunistic Beach Fill Program (OBFP) and Sand Compatibility and Opportunistic Use Program (SCOUP)" authorizing the City Manager, or their designee, in coordination with the City Attorney, to execute a 15-year lease agreement with the California State Lands Commission to allow continued sand nourishment along the Encinitas coast, consistent with the locations set through the Opportunistic Beach Fill Program (OBFP) and Sand Compatibility and Opportunistic Use Program (SCOUP).
2024-12-11 Item 08F Opportunistic Beach Fill Lease

("Interwest") to add $120,000 for additional support with as-needed civil engineering services for private land development projects. The actions involve organizational or administrative activities of government that will not result in the direct or indirect physical change in the environment. Contact Person: Principal Engineer Cabrera
1) Authorize the City Manager or her designee, in coordination with the City Attorney, to execute Amendment No. 2 to the Agreement with Interwest in substantial form, to add $120,000 of capacity to the professional consultant contract, for a new not-to-exceed amount of $415,000; and 2) Adopt City Council Resolution No. 2024-131, titled "A Resolution of the City Council of the City of Encinitas, California, Amending the Fiscal Year 2024-25 Budget" to appropriate $120,000 to the Land Development Division Professional Services Budget.
2024-12-11 Item 08G Interwest As-Needed Civil Engineering Services Amendment 2

(CASE NO. SUB-007085; APN: 260-305-11)"

PROCEDURES FOR PUBLIC HEARINGS ON APPEALS (ITEM 10A and 10B): New information such as documents, exhibits, letters, photos, charts, diagrams, videos, etc., WILL NOT be considered by the City Council if presented at this meeting. All material must have been submitted to the City Clerk no less than 7 calendar days prior to this hearing.

10A.
Public hearing to consider a timely-filed appeal (Case No. APPEAL-007691-2024) of the Planning Commission's approval of a density bonus and design review permit authorizing the construction of an 87-unit apartment project (Camino Apartments) and associated improvements on a 1.93 gross acre site. The project is located on the east side of El Camino Real and north of Garden View Road. Contact Person: Senior Planner Danna
This agenda item has been removed from the agenda and will be rescheduled and renoticed for the regular meeting of January 15, 2025. It only appears on the agenda because it was legally noticed.
10B.
Public hearing to consider a timely-filed appeal (Case No. APPEAL-007676-2024) of the Planning Commission's approval of a density bonus, tentative map, design review permit, and coastal development permit authorizing a 17-lot density bonus subdivision with associated site, grading, and public improvements, located on Bella Vista Drive (APN: 216-122-17).). Environmental Considerations: Pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), an Environmental Initial Study (IS) was conducted which determined that the proposed project may have significant environmental effects related to aesthetics, biological resources, cultural resources, geology (paleontological resources), and tribal cultural resources. The project, with incorporation of the specific mitigation measures set forth in the approval, avoid or mitigate the potential significant environmental impacts to a less than significant level. A Mitigated Negative Declaration (MND) and Mitigation Monitoring and Reporting Program (MMRP) was prepared for the proposed project and adopted by the Planning Commission. Contact Person: Assistant Director of Development Services Colamussi
Deny the appeal and adopt the attached draft City Council Resolution No. 2024-129 titled "A Resolution of the City Council of the City of Encinitas, California Denying the Appeal Filed by United Citizens for Responsible Development of Bella Vista and Affirming the Planning Commission's Decision Approving a Density Bonus, Tentative Map, Design Review Permit, and Coastal Development Permit Authorizing the Subdivision of One (1) Existing Lot Into 17 Residential Lots (15 Market Rate and Two "Very-Low" Affordable Lots) and One (1) Private Street Lot Utilizing the State Density Bonus Law; Construction of One (1) Private Cul-De-Sac Road (Lot A), Grading to Exceed Four (4) Feet of Fill and Eight (8) Feet of Cut, and Landscape, Utility, Stormwater Drainage, and Site/Public Improvements; Encroachment Into Steep Slopes; and Use of a Construction Trailer, for Property Located on Bella Vista Drive (APN: 216-122-17) (CASE NOS. APPEAL-007676-2024, MULTI-005107-2022, SUB-005109-2022, DR-005108-2022, CDPNF-005602-2022; APN: 216-122-17)" affirming the Planning Commission's decision to adopt Resolution No. 2024-31 approving the density bonus, tentative map, design review permit, and coastal development permit (Case Nos. MULTI-005107-2022, SUB-005109-2022, DR-005108-2022, CDPNF-005602-2022) with conditions.

SANDAG Update on the Batiquitos Lagoon Double Tracking Project, and Requests related to City-Owned Parcels at La Costa Avenue and N. Coast Highway 101. Environmental Considerations: The action being considered by the City Council is exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) because it is not a "project" under Section 15378(b)(5) of CEQA Guidelines. SANDAG has filed a Notice of Exemption for the BLDT project, State Clearing House Number 2024061076. Contact Person: Director of Engineering Bankston
1) Receive Update from SANDAG on the Batiquitos Lagoon Double Tracking Project (BLDT); 2) Authorize SANDAG access to the BLDT project site on North County Transit District (NCTD) parcels through City-owned Parcels at La Costa Avenue and N. Notice to the Public:
To ensure that the City meets your needs when addressing the City Council, all presentation materials which require the use of visual equipment need to be submitted to the City's IT Division at least 24 hours in advance of the meeting (except for appeal hearings where materials must be submitted 7 days in advance). This includes photographs, Microsoft Office documents (PowerPoint, Word, Excel). No CD's, DVD's, or USB thumb/flash drives will be accepted at the meeting. All materials must be in PC format and digital presentation items must be emailed to it-service-desk@encinitasca.gov . Please label all materials with the corresponding agenda item number. Should technical assistance be necessary, it will be available to presenters from 5:30 p.m. to 5:50 p.m. on the day of the meeting. Presentation of video/digital/photographs are considered part of the maximum time limit provided to speakers.
